title: The Summer of Rosewater Lane
premise: Marine biologist Jude Crane returns to her coastal hometown of Merrow Point to settle her late grandmother's estate, expecting paperwork and a quick exit. Instead she finds an undelivered letter, postmarked eleven years ago, from Eli Navarro — the boy she loved and left without explanation — revealing that her grandmother intercepted it to keep Jude on the path she'd chosen for her. As Jude and Eli, now the town's struggling harbormaster, excavate the truth of what was taken from them both, they must decide whether a love built on stolen years can be rebuilt on honesty. In the end, Jude chooses to stay — not as penance or inheritance, but as her own act of will — and delivers her grandmother's final letter to Eli herself, closing the circle.
about_author: Astrid Okonkwo is a former tide-pool educator who writes love stories set where the water meets memory. She lives in a converted boathouse with her partner and an opinionated gull named Reginald.

chapters.title: The Estate of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She arrives in Merrow Point to inventory her grandmother's house, treating grief like a logistics problem. The beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack as familiar rooms ambush her with memory.

chapters.title: Turtles Don't Write Letters
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Sorting papers, she finds a sealed letter addressed to her, postmarked eleven years ago, never opened. She recognizes the handwriting instantly. Beat: dread and longing colliding; she can't bring herself to read it yet.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She finally reads Eli's letter — a proposal, a plan, a future — and realizes her grandmother hid it. Flashback threads reveal the summer they lost. Beat: betrayal reframes her whole history of 'choosing' science over love.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli sees Jude's car at the Crane house and steels himself. Their first encounter at the dock is polite, loaded, and brief. Beat: old wounds presented as new small talk; neither says what matters.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She volunteers to help survey the bay's turtle nests, forcing proximity with Eli's crew. Work becomes their only honest language. Beat: cautious thaw, competence as flirtation, first almost-laugh together.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Digging through estate records, she finds evidence her grandmother meddled more than once — letters returned, calls screened, opportunities quietly rerouted. Beat: anger curdling into a darker question: how much of her life was authored by someone else?

chapters.title: Concessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli admits to his sister Rosa that he never stopped waiting, and that Jude's return feels like cruelty dressed as chance. Beat: vulnerability; we learn the harbor is failing financially and Eli may lose everything he stayed for.

chapters.title: The Nest Count
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm threatens a loggerhead nest; Jude and Eli work all night relocating eggs. Drenched, exhausted, they nearly kiss. Beat: intimacy rekindling under emergency conditions; the past briefly irrelevant.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude offers Eli exactly what she once gave: fragments, no promises, no future talk. He refuses — he won't be trained to want less. Beat: rejection that stings because he's right; her containment strategy exposed.

chapters.title: Rosa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa reveals that after Jude left, Eli spiraled, and their mother's illness went untreated because money went to keeping the boat afloat. Beat: Jude confronts the cost others paid for her absence; guilt with teeth.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Among the ledger pages, Jude finds a second envelope — unopened, in her grandmother's hand, addressed to Eli. Her grandmother wrote him too. Beat: escalation; the inheritance of secrets deepens, and Jude must choose whether to open it.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The letter reveals her grandmother's own abandoned love, and her belief that she was saving Jude from the same heartbreak. Power wielded as protection. Beat: complicated grief — understanding without forgiving.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Crane House
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli learns about the intercepted letter from Rosa and storms the house mid-inventory. He and Jude fight — eleven years of it — ugly and necessary. Beat: climax of resentment; truths said that can't be unsaid.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A research institute offers Jude her dream posting in Costa Rica — the life her grandmother engineered her toward. Deadline: two weeks. Beat: the old script vs. the new possibility; power of choice finally hers.

chapters.title: Harbor Lights
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli, resigned to losing her again, begins selling the family boat to save the harbor. Jude finds him saying goodbye to it. Beat: quiet devastation; two people grieving futures separately.

chapters.title: Risking the Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude stops counting reasons and tells Eli everything — the letter, the ledger, her fear, her fault. No negotiation, no pieces. Beat: full vulnerability; the emotional summit before the plot climax.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the harbor auction, an out-of-town developer bids to raze the docks. Jude publicly pledges her inheritance to match the bid — betting the estate, and her standing in town, on staying. Beat: action climax; love made visible as commitment.

chapters.title: Delivering the Letter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude hand-delivers her grandmother's letter to Eli and reads it aloud with him — apology, blessing, and a request for forgiveness addressed to them both. Beat: catharsis; the dead released, the living freed.

chapters.title: Costa Rica, Declined
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude declines the posting but negotiates a remote partnership so she keeps her science — choosing Merrow Point without shrinking herself. Beat: agency reclaimed; inheritance redefined as what you build, not what you're given.

chapters.title: Hatchlings
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The relocated nest hatches at dawn; the whole town watches the turtles make for the water. Eli takes Jude's hand in front of everyone. Beat: public reconciliation; tenderness after storm.

chapters.title: Rosewater Lane, Renumbered
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli shows Jude the house on Rosewater Lane he bought back years ago, always meaning to send word. They begin renovating it together. Beat: hope made domestic; the future getting walls and windows.

chapters.title: A Trainable Heart
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. One year later: harbor thriving, nest surveys ongoing, a wedding invitation written on the back of an old unsent letter. Jude reflects that the heart, like any muscle, grows strongest under honest load. Beat: resolution — love as practice, not accident.
